Employee attrition is an important concern for organizations because losing employees can lead to increased recruitment and training expenses, reduced productivity, and the loss of experienced team members. Understanding which employee characteristics are associated with attrition can help organizations make more informed decisions about employee retention.

The purpose of this case study is to analyze employee data to identify patterns associated with attrition and evaluate whether machine learning models can predict which employees are likely to leave. Using a dataset containing 870 employees, the analysis explores relationships between attrition and factors such as job role, job satisfaction, overtime, monthly income, and years of experience.

The study begins with exploratory data analysis to examine differences between employees who stayed and those who left. Next, two classification models, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) and Naive Bayes, are developed and evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity. Finally, a cost analysis estimates the potential financial impact of using these models to guide retention efforts. The overall goal is to determine whether predictive modeling can provide useful insights for developing more targeted and cost-effective employee retention strategies.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(e1071)
library(class)
library(caret)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)
```

```{r}
# slide 2 :attrition rate 16%

attrition_summary = data %>%
  count(Attrition) %>%
  mutate(Percentage = n / sum(n), Label = paste0(n, " (", percent(Percentage, accuracy = 0.1),
  ")"))

attrition_summary

ggplot(attrition_summary, aes(x = Attrition, y = n, fill = Attrition)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = Label), vjust = -0.4, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "gray", "Yes" = "#daaa96")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +

    title = "Employee Attrition in the Dataset",

    y = "Number of Employees"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
```

```{r}
dept_summary = data %>%
```

```{r}

model_data = subset(data, select = -c(ID, EmployeeNumber, EmployeeCount, Over18, 
                                      StandardHours, JobLevel, YearsSinceLastPromotion))

model_data$Attrition = factor(model_data$Attrition, levels = c("No", "Yes"))

categorical_vars = c(
  "BusinessTravel", "Department", "Education",
  "EducationField", "EnvironmentSatisfaction",
  "Gender", "JobInvolvement", "JobLevel",
  "JobRole", "JobSatisfaction", "MaritalStatus",
  "OverTime", "PerformanceRating",
  "RelationshipSatisfaction", "StockOptionLevel",
  "WorkLifeBalance"
)

categorical_vars = intersect(categorical_vars, names(model_data))

for (v in categorical_vars) {
  model_data[[v]] = factor(model_data[[v]])}

set.seed(13)

train_indices = sample(seq_len(nrow(model_data)), round(0.8 * nrow(model_data)))
train_data = model_data[train_indices, ]
test_data = model_data[-train_indices, ]

```

```{r}
# find optimal k for knn
library(class)
library(caret)

set.seed(13)

iterations = 500
numks = 90
splitPerc = .80

masterAcc = matrix(nrow = iterations, ncol = numks)
masterSens = matrix(nrow = iterations, ncol = numks)
masterSpec = matrix(nrow = iterations, ncol = numks)

# Convert categorical predictors to factors
categorical_vars = c(
  "BusinessTravel", "Department", "Education",
  "EducationField", "EnvironmentSatisfaction", "Gender",
  "JobInvolvement", "JobLevel", "JobRole",
  "JobSatisfaction", "MaritalStatus", "OverTime",
  "PerformanceRating", "RelationshipSatisfaction",
  "StockOptionLevel", "WorkLifeBalance"
)

categorical_vars = intersect(categorical_vars, names(model_data))

for (v in categorical_vars) {
  print(table(model_data[[v]], useNA = "ifany"))
}

for (v in categorical_vars) {
  model_data[[v]] = factor(model_data[[v]])
}

for (j in 1:iterations) {
  
  trainIndices = sample(1:nrow(model_data), round(splitPerc * nrow(model_data)))
  
  train = model_data[trainIndices, ]
  test = model_data[-trainIndices, ]
  
  train_y = train$Attrition
  test_y = test$Attrition
  
  predictor_names = setdiff(names(train), "Attrition")
  
  # dummy encode categorical variables using training data
  dummy_model = dummyVars(
    ~ .,
    data = train[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE],
    fullRank = TRUE
  )
  
  train_x = predict(
    dummy_model,
    newdata = train[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE]
  )
  
  test_x = predict(
    dummy_model,
    newdata = test[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE]
  )
  
  # remove near-zero-variance predictors
  nzv = nearZeroVar(train_x)
  
  if (length(nzv) > 0) {
    train_x = train_x[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
    test_x = test_x[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
  }
  
  # ccale using training means and std deviations
  train_means = colMeans(train_x)
  train_sds = apply(train_x, 2, sd)
  
  # remove columns with zero or invalid standard deviation
  valid_cols = is.finite(train_sds) & train_sds > 0
  
  train_x = train_x[, valid_cols, drop = FALSE]
  test_x = test_x[, valid_cols, drop = FALSE]
  
  train_means = train_means[valid_cols]
  train_sds = train_sds[valid_cols]
  
  train_x = scale(
    train_x,
    center = train_means,
    scale = train_sds
  )
  
  test_x = scale(
    test_x,
    center = train_means,
    scale = train_sds
  )
  
  # test each value of k
  for (i in 1:numks) {
    
    classifications = knn(
      train = train_x,
      test = test_x,
      cl = train_y,
      prob = TRUE,
      k = i
    )
    
    CM = confusionMatrix(
      data = factor(classifications, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
      reference = factor(test_y, levels = c("No", "Yes")),
      positive = "Yes"
    )
    
    masterAcc[j, i] = CM$overall["Accuracy"]
    masterSens[j, i] = CM$byClass["Sensitivity"]
    masterSpec[j, i] = CM$byClass["Specificity"]
  }
}

MeanAcc = colMeans(masterAcc, na.rm = TRUE)
MeanSens = colMeans(masterSens, na.rm = TRUE)
MeanSpec = colMeans(masterSpec, na.rm = TRUE)

# plot(
#  seq(1, numks, 1),
#  MeanAcc,
#  type = "l",
#  xlab = "k",
#  ylab = "Mean Accuracy",
#  main = "KNN Accuracy vs. k"
# ghvn)

plot(
  1:numks,
  MeanSens,
  type = "l",
  xlab = "k",
  ylab = "Mean Sensitivity",
  main = "KNN Sensitivity vs. k"
)

# Best k based on mean accuracy
# best_k = which.max(MeanAcc)
# MeanAcc[best_k]

best_k_sens = which.max(MeanSens)
best_k_sens
MeanSens[best_k_sens]
```

```{r}
# knn model

train_y = train_data$Attrition
test_y = test_data$Attrition

predictor_names = setdiff(names(train_data), "Attrition")


# dummy encode categorical variables
dummy_model = dummyVars(~ .,data = train_data[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE], fullRank = TRUE)

train_x = predict(dummy_model, newdata = train_data[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE])

test_x = predict(dummy_model, newdata = test_data[, predictor_names, drop = FALSE])

# remove near-zero-variance predictors
nzv = nearZeroVar(train_x)

if (length(nzv) > 0) {
  train_x = train_x[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
  test_x = test_x[, -nzv, drop = FALSE]
}

# scale using training data only

train_sds = apply(train_x, 2, sd)
valid_cols = is.finite(train_sds) & train_sds > 0

train_x = train_x[, valid_cols, drop = FALSE]
test_x = test_x[, valid_cols, drop = FALSE]

train_means = colMeans(train_x)
train_sds = apply(train_x, 2, sd)

train_x = scale(train_x, center = train_means, scale = train_sds)
test_x = scale(test_x, center = train_means, scale = train_sds)

# fit knn
classifications = knn(train = train_x, test = test_x, cl = train_y, prob = TRUE, k = 3)

# evaluate model
knn_prob_yes = ifelse(classifications == "Yes", winning_vote, 1 - winning_vote)

threshold = 0.20

knn_predictions = factor(ifelse(knn_prob_yes >= threshold, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))

CM_knn = confusionMatrix(
  data = knn_predictions,
  reference = test_y,
  positive = "Yes")

CM_knn
```
